item.title: Here's what the numbers show about key races 4 days ahead of midterms
item.description: Zach Donnini, head of data science at VoteHub, joins "The Takeout" to break down the latest numbers with midterms just a couple of days away.

item.title: Gen Z turns to books and puzzles to reduce time spent doomscrolling
item.description: A new trend called "brain stacking" is encouraging Gen Zers to spend less time on their phones. Crystal Bell, digital culture editor at Mashable, joins "The Daily Report" to share more.

item.title: Inside Philly's "House of Horrors" | Case by Case | "48 Hours" Podcast
item.description: House of Horrors or House of Mirrors? A routine traffic stop led investigators to the Philadelphia property now dubbed by neighbors as a "House of Horrors." "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and "48 Hours" consultant and investigator Herman Weisberg break down the conflicting and disturbing evidence authorities uncovered at the home of the late Raymond C. Horsch, including clues that families hope will shed new light on the disappearance of his ex-wife, Amy McHale, and six other missing women.

item.title: How Florida voters are reacting to Democrat Angie Nixon's progressive stances
item.description: President Trump is campaigning in Florida as CBS News rates the state's highly watched Senate race as likely Republican. CBS News contributor Marc Caputo has more.

item.title: Cost of caring for an elderly parent rising faster than inflation, study finds
item.description: The cost of caring for an elderly loved one has been rising faster than inflation, up 60% since 2021, according to a study by AARP. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has the story.

item.title: Top DOJ attorney in Alaska calls Alaska Senate allegations "troubling"
item.description: The top federal prosecutor in Alaska did not specify what crimes are being investigated by the Justice Department, saying he's "not making any assumptions on whether a crime has been committed or not."

item.title: Trump says Iran war will end "soon" as Qatar pushes for U.S.-Iran deal
item.description: President Trump claims his war with Iran will come to an end "soon" as Qatari mediators push for a deal days before the midterms. CBS News senior national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata breaks it down.

item.title: Why Trump is spending time campaigning in deep red Florida
item.description: President Trump is set to appear at rally in Daytona Beach, Florida, on Friday night. This also comes after Mr. Trump reversed course on his decision to cancel upcoming weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa. CBS News correspondent Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: Alaska voters weigh in on Dan Sullivan controversy as DOJ investigates
item.description: Alaska voters are reacting to the state's Dan Sullivan controversy amid the Justice Department's investigation into whether crimes were committed. CBS News' Taurean Small is there and has the story.

item.title: Trump predicts Iran war will end soon as Qatar pushes for a deal
item.description: Trump predicts the war with Iran is "going to end soon," without offering any details, as Qatari mediators return to Tehran to push for a deal.

item.title: Latest on midterms as campaigns make final push
item.description: Adam Mockler, host of "The Adam Mocker Show," and Elizabeth Pipko, former RNC spokesperson and host of "Made in America with Elizabeth Pipko," join "The Takeout" to discuss the upcoming midterms.

item.title: ATF's top lawyer, who oversaw overhaul of its firearms regulations, resigns
item.description: Robert Leider was appointed as the ATF's top attorney last year, shortly after former Attorney General Pam Bondi abruptly fired the agency's former chief, claiming without evidence that the bureau was "targeting gun owners."

item.title: Interview with Alaska independent congressional candidate
item.description: Bill Hill, an independent candidate for Congress from Alaska, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign and the multiple controversies surrounding the state's electoral process.

item.title: Trump to hold rallies in Kansas and Iowa despite earlier cancelation
item.description: President Trump has been going back and forth on whether he will hold rallies in Kansas and Iowa scheduled for this weekend. Florida State Senator Joe Gruters joins "The Takeout" to share his thoughts.

item.title: How hard is it to recover the $6 billion stolen from Binance?
item.description: Security experts are calling it the "largest bank robbery in human history." Getting all of the stolen crypto funds won't be easy.

item.title: South Carolina Senate race now leans Republican, CBS News data desk says
item.description: South Carolina's Senate race is now leaning Republican, according to new analysis from the CBS News data desk. CBS News' executive director of elections and surveys, Anthony Salvanto, breaks down the numbers.

item.title: How Trump's immigration policies are impacting voting in Texas border races
item.description: Trump' immigration policies are having an impact on voters in Texas' border communities as midterms approach. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the story.

item.title: Midterm Updates: Trump heading to Florida for rally as election nears
item.description: The November 2026 midterm elections are just four days away. Candidates in key races — and President Trump — are making their closing arguments to voters.

item.title: Alaska voters react to Mary Peltola's campaign's alleged role in Dan Sullivan controversy
item.description: Alaska's Senate race is under investigation amid claims that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign recruited a candidate who shares a name with Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. CBS News' Taurean Small is in Anchorage, Alaska, where voters are reacting.

item.title: Why Trump is campaigning for Republicans in deep red Florida
item.description: President Donald Trump is campaigning for Republicans in Florida this Friday with only a couple of days to go until the midterms. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has the details.

item.title: Nasdaq sheds more than 700 points as tech stocks slump
item.description: Disappointing earnings reports from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel renewed fears on Friday that the AI trade could unravel.

item.title: Kansas Secretary of State explains process to verify citizenship of voters
item.description: Scott Schwab, Kansas' secretary of state, joins CBS News to discuss the upcoming midterms and the state's process for verifying the citizenship of voters.

item.title: Trump reverses course on canceling rallies in Kansas and Iowa this weekend
item.description: President Trump reversed course on his decision to cancel this weekend's rallies in Kansas and Iowa. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more.

item.title: Watch: DOJ officials hold press conference on Alaska Dan Sullivan controversy
item.description: Officials from the Department of Justice held a press conference on the ongoing investigation into the Dan Sullivan case in Alaska on Friday. CBS News' Nicole Sganga breaks down the key takeaways.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz routes remain clear, CENTCOM chief claims
item.description: The head of U.S. Central Command says that Iran's navy is destroyed and that the main Strait of Hormuz routes are clear. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has more information.

item.title: Watch: Trump takes questions on Iran War, Venezuela, midterms, more
item.description: President Trump took reporters' questions in the Oval Office on Friday on topics ranging from potential sanctions against Russia to the Iran War and the midterms. Standing next to him was Stephen Hubbard, an American recently released from a Russian prison.

item.title: Daniel J. Sullivan left his Alaska hometown before Senate election
item.description: Daniel J. Sullivan, the independent Alaska Senate candidate whose name is almost identical to the Republican incumbent, left his hometown of Petersburg earlier this week, multiple sources confirmed to CBS News.

item.title: Trump meets with Stephen Hubbard after release from Russian jail
item.description: Stephen Hubbard was imprisoned in Russia for over four years until gaining release last week.

item.title: Internal documents show failed scramble to save "forever cruise"
item.description: The MV Odyssey was billed as a continuous around-the-world cruise when it launched in October 2024. It ended abruptly in Cambodia.

item.title: From the archives: Patrick Stewart on "Star Trek" and Shakespeare
item.description: Sir Patrick Stewart, the classically-trained stage actor who was best-known for his roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises, died on Oct. 28, 2026 at age 86. In this "Sunday Morning" profile that aired May 24, 2020, Stewart talked with CBS News' Tony Dokoupil about returning to the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the TV series "Star Trek: Picard," and about how he sought an escape from the COVID pandemic through the Bard's poetry.
